newsitem.title: BRAZIL: RESEARCH ALERT-Cemig downgraded to hold.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT-Cemig downgraded to hold.

text.p: Credit Lyonnais Securities Inc said in a report it was lowering its recommendation for Minas Gerais state power firm Cemig to hold from buy.
-- "The shares have outperformed the market by about 10 percent over the past month and we see limited further upside," Credit Lyonnais analyst Rosana Aldworth wrote.
-- She said Cemig could be hurt by the restructuring of Brazil's electrical sector and its stock already reflects the improved prospects from private participation in management.

-- A consortium led by U.S.-based AES Corp and Southern Electric in late May bought a 32.96 percent voting stake in Cemig for the base price of 1.13 billion reais ($1.0 billion) but the firm remains under state control.
-- "New policies and effective gains in efficiency and profitability will take at least a few months to show results," Aldworth said.

-- She said that, as a fully integrated electric utility, Cemig is likely to be hurt by the proposed new sector model if limits are imposed on the sale of Cemig's own generated energy to final consumers.
-- "Although the proposed model will face political opposition, and has yet to be approved by the executive, it lends uncertainty to Cemig's prospects," she added.

-- Credit Lyonnais lowered its EBIT estimates for Cemig for the period 1997-2000 by 1.5 percent, 6.8 percent, 1.7 percent and 1.2 percent, but raised inflation-adjusted forecasts due to higher-than-expected monetary correction, she added.
-- Cemig preferred was off 0.92 percent at 54.10 reais and its common was up 0.2 percent at 49.10 reais at 1120 local time/1420 GMT on the Sao Paulo bourse.
